subproblem.title: Antilipschitz charts pull back Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ and c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 we have Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ Z : Set (Eucl P), (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) Z = 0 → (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' Z) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the estimate of step 1 of the parent proof: Ψ = (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ is (1/c)-Lipschitz, so it maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ(Ω) to Lⁿ-null sets (Lⁿ(Ψ(Z)) ≤ c^{−n} Hⁿ(Z)).

1. Φ is injective on Ω: if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω then c|w − w′| ≤ 0, so |w − w′| = 0 since c > 0.
2. If Ω = ∅, then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise ℝⁿ is nonempty and Ψ := Function.invFunOn Φ Ω satisfies Ψ(Φ(w)) = w for all w ∈ Ω (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn).
3. Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω): for y = Φ(w), y′ = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω, |Ψ(y) − Ψ(y′)| = |w − w′| ≤ c⁻¹|Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| = c⁻¹|y − y′| (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul with constant Real.toNNReal c⁻¹).
4. Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) ⊆ Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)): if w ∈ Ω and Φ(w) ∈ Z then Φ(w) ∈ Z ∩ Φ(Ω) and Ψ(Φ(w)) = w.
5. Lipschitz maps increase Hⁿ by at most the n-th power of the constant (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, scaled by the normalizing factor of μHE[n]; packaged as SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, which is in scope): Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z) = 0.
6. On ℝⁿ, Lⁿ = Hⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By monotonicity and steps 4–5, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = Hⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) ≤ Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz with c > 0 gives injectivity on Ω; Ψ := invFunOn Φ Ω is a left inverse on Ω.
Hⁿ Lipschitz image bound (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn) gives Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0.

audit.reason: Exact contract match. Positive antilipschitzness gives an inverse Lipschitz map. Its Hausdorff image bound and Hⁿ = volume on Eucl n prove the pullback is null. No additional measurability of Ω, Φ, or Z is needed.
